paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this one. At twelve years old, Jesus is in the temple courts, listening to the teachers and asking them questions (Luke 2:46). Then He tells His parents He had to be in "My Father's house" (Luke 2:49). Even at twelve, He knows whose house that is, and that's where He belongs.

Now look at what happens next, because it's quiet and it matters. His parents don't understand what He's saying (Luke 2:50), and I think that's okay, friend. You don't have to get every line of God's Word on the first read. Mary doesn't walk away. She treasures "all these things in her heart" (Luke 2:51), and that's a pretty good plan for any baker who hits a verse that won't make sense yet.

And then Jesus goes home. He goes down to Nazareth and is "obedient to them" (Luke 2:51), and He keeps growing "in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and man" (Luke 2:52). So the Son who belongs in His Father's house also grows up slowly, one ordinary day at a time. Friend, you're allowed to grow that way too, and I'm cheering for every inch of it.
